candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.source_attribution: 1 Enoch 18:14, trans. R.H. Charles (1912). PD. Cf. Jude 1:13.
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

The angel-guide tells Enoch: 'This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven' — the prison of the fallen stars. The 'stars' here are angelic beings (per ancient Near Eastern cosmology where stars are the visible counterparts of heavenly powers); the prison is where the Watcher-stars who transgressed are confined awaiting judgment. Jude 1:13's 'wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever' Tewahedo reads as direct allusion to this Enochic verse. The cosmology of stars-as-angels is preserved in Tewahedo liturgical hymnody.
